title: Prove sharp Gaussian radial budgets for every finite iterate identity
body:
**This scoped theorem gives the sharp radial budget for every prescribed finite Gaussian iterate identity.** For a total Gaussian-pair map with exact sum, Euclidean error at most one from the positive half-transform and `F^m=id`, four must divide m. Let R be the first odd integer at least five that does not divide m. The exact minimum forward outward slack is `sqrt((R^2+2R+3)/2)-sqrt((R^2+1)/2)`. **No new kappa** follows.

Read the [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ba5e006ed70119b23d6ef9e2e8627e43a3f4f18b/research/gaussian-finite-iterate-optimum/PROOF.md), [receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ba5e006ed70119b23d6ef9e2e8627e43a3f4f18b/research/gaussian-finite-iterate-optimum/RESULT.json), [local map and checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ba5e006ed70119b23d6ef9e2e8627e43a3f4f18b/research/gaussian-finite-iterate-optimum/verify.py) and [credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ba5e006ed70119b23d6ef9e2e8627e43a3f4f18b/research/gaussian-finite-iterate-optimum/CREDITS.md).

At m=20 the optimum is `sqrt(33)-5`; at m=140 it is `sqrt(51)-sqrt(41)`. The known m=4 value `sqrt(19)-sqrt(13)` remains prior work. Finite iterate budgets approach `1/sqrt(2)` as their compatible odd ring periods increase, while every fixed finite m has a strict gap above that limit. The requirement is an iterate identity, not that m be the least positive global period. The constructed map's least period can be smaller.

The lower proof isolates the first incompatible ring between two invariant finite squares. It assumes no symmetry. The upper construction combines directed single-ring cycles with shifted annular pairs and handles a separate central case when three does not divide m. It is total on every sum fiber and both half-grid colors, has an explicit inverse, and attains the same sharp bound for forward, inverse outward and absolute radial change. Its local point rule uses no unbounded matching table. A four-cycle supplies exact attainment after the all-input upper proof is established.

This resolves the general finite-iterate optimum left open in [PR #7699](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7699). No native tariff, selected caller, tensor commutation, inverse-by-conjugation contract, scratch restoration or complete recursive invoice is supplied. The selected kappa stays `0.00363005817`, with all five assumptions retained. Exact least period, extra state, larger blocks and changed sum/error contracts remain outside scope.

With CPython 3.12 and its standard library:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-finite-iterate-optimum
```

Both registered normal and optimized commands print:

```text
PASS_GAUSSIAN_FINITE_ITERATE_OPTIMUM
1024 iterate budgets; 23 complete grids; 41032 half-grid points
2424 lower-boundary edges; 19208 full Gaussian inputs; all controls pass
```

Twenty-three complete grids cover 20 critical cutoffs from five through 61, including both central choices at R=5,7,9. A separate arc generator agrees with the local map. Direct traversal checks every cycle and its order; all inverses, unit edges, both colors, exact radial inequalities and attaining cycles pass. The 2424 exterior edges of the critical square pairs meet the lower threshold. Another 19208 Gaussian inputs cover all component parities and eight iterate choices. All arithmetic is integral with certified square-root comparisons.

Omitting the central annular case fails m=4,20,140. Leaving the first incompatible ring as a single ring fails the required iterate. Reusing the unchanged fourth-power construction exceeds the new m=20 budget. The zero-sum control has exact period four. The all-m and all-input claims rest on the written proof; finite cycles and grids are corroboration.

Normal/optimized replay, committed bytes and modes, source history, export and sealed Git-free replay pass. Hosted CI did not certify this package. The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44337137005/job/134916780270) failed in the shared `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the base guide names frontier6030 while the selected record requires `make frontier7000-verify`. The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence. Full predecessor suites, selected cold replay, native/physical replay, Lean, Docker, independent human and formal-kernel review were not run. The adapted checker is not an independent source review.

Credit Jerry Chen (@CubeJerry) for the half-grid, annular matching and sharp square-to-swap construction in [PR #7570](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7570), head `053c42c68165cf24fd4e8bc33c2b20d6ac3d399b`: [all-input proof](https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/blob/053c42c68165cf24fd4e8bc33c2b20d6ac3d399b/research/sharp-order-four-gaussian-rounding/proof/PROOF.md). The annular formula and connector cycle are adapted to new starting radii; its m=4 optimum is retained.

Ali Romman's [PR #7699](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7699), head `2a5dcb314ccdfeed24bd86ec1f56f519eead56c1`, supplies the [ring classification and finite-order lower framework](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2a5dcb314ccdfeed24bd86ec1f56f519eead56c1/research/gaussian-radial-order-classification/PROOF.md) and [adapted exact comparison routines](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2a5dcb314ccdfeed24bd86ec1f56f519eead56c1/research/gaussian-radial-order-classification/verify.py). Its [source credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/2a5dcb314ccdfeed24bd86ec1f56f519eead56c1/research/gaussian-radial-order-classification/CREDITS.md) retain the global-optimum, provider, earlier Gaussian and Nick Petalas exact-sum contributions. Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0.

Live handoffs, current source heads, source-reference intake, phrase overlap and the closed delta were checked. Sparse local and unpublished work remain coverage limits. No follow-up is reserved.
